# Decantr

> AI Frontend Governance for production codebases touched by AI agents. Decantr defines contracts, route-scoped context, graph-backed evidence, and repair prompts around AI-edited frontend code.

## Current Product Model

Decantr 3.9 is content-first and governance-first. Its Governed Change Proof model composes `AdoptionTruthV1`, `TaskCapsuleV1`, and `GovernanceDeltaV1` around existing Project Health and typed graph evidence. `@decantr/verifier` owns those three contracts. Existing report-producing commands stay on their v2 schemas by default; only `decantr ci --report-version v3` and an explicitly generated v3 CI workflow emit `decantr-ci-report.v3`.

The official corpus, client, resolver, ranking, wiring, and content provenance implementations live in `@decantr/content` inside the monorepo. The public `registry.decantr.ai` marketplace/portal is retired. `@decantr/registry` is a thin Decantr 3.x compatibility facade over content-owned implementations; `decantr registry ...`, `REGISTRY_URL`, and MCP `decantr_registry` remain compatibility names.

`@decantr/css` is a legacy optional adapter. Greenfield and Brownfield defaults are contract-only unless `--adoption=decantr-css` is explicit.

Studio is a local read-only renderer: it may recompute current state in memory or read project-mode Project Health v2 and CI v2/v3 artifacts, but it does not write source/contracts/baselines or execute adoption, repair, migration, build, verification, package-manager, or agent workflows.

The 3.9 route/source and machine evidence lanes are complete: 84 frozen route cases, 24 genuine competing forbidden sources, a supplemental pinned Angular Brownfield replay across 43 route signals/35 taskable pages/62 components, and 270 isolated machine samples. The two-human 200-finding adjudication lane remains incomplete. Stable 3.9.3 publishes through the explicit sole-maintainer waiver, but that does not authorize human precision, recall, release-qualification, or adoption-proven claims.

## Operational Notes

- For app-scoped monorepos, pass `--project <app>` to `doctor`, `check`, `verify`, `ci`, `task`, `resolve`, `codify`, and `graph`.
- Greenfield `init` and Brownfield `adopt` write the first typed graph; shared discovery supplies route/source provenance even without Brownfield analysis.
- Angular discovery is production-entry based: selected `angular.json`/`project.json` build entry -> bootstrap import graph -> router root -> nested/lazy route arrays -> rendered component. Tests/fixtures are excluded, lazy boundaries are not taskable pages, Tailwind dependency presence is not styling authority, and authority/completeness are independent from score.
- Angular Brownfield `adopt`/existing `init` refuse unproven or partial route authority unless `--force` is explicit. CLI/MCP route tasks and CI v3 still fail closed with `DISCOVERY_NOT_PROVEN`/`not_proven`; an override does not create proof.
- `decantr task` and MCP task context require current graph artifacts and adapt one `TaskCapsuleV1`; the required rank-one read target is the discovered route implementation source. The default canonical capsule is bounded to 12,000 UTF-8 bytes and 4,000 deterministic estimated tokens. Blocked CLI task activation emits remediation and exits nonzero.
- MCP task responses default to compact detail. Pass `"detail": "full"` only when full graph nodes, edges, and expanded context are required.
- `scan --json`, Project Health, Evidence Bundle, workspace health, and ordinary `decantr ci` remain v2. Use `decantr ci --report-version v3 --since <ref> --json` only when `AdoptionTruthV1` plus `GovernanceDeltaV1` are required. Missing/stale/incompatible proof is `not_proven`, not an empty delta.
- `decantr ci init` generates v2 by default. Add `--report-version v3` explicitly; GitHub v3 workflows fetch full history and pass a resolved change base through `--since`.
- Accept reviewed local law with `decantr codify --accept --confirm-reviewed`. Add `--accept-style-bridge` only to explicitly activate a reviewed bridge proposal.
- Saved Brownfield health baselines keep inherited findings visible while project CI gates only new findings through the v2 `baselineGate` block. CI v3 additionally classifies stable finding occurrences as new, inherited, resolved, or unclassified and fails closed when proof is incomplete.
- Assistant bridges follow their recorded workflow and available content: contract-only Greenfield uses Essence, narrative context, and the Contract capsule; corpus-backed Greenfield/Hybrid uses packs; Brownfield uses analysis/doctrine plus available context. Prettier/Oxfmt projects ignore generated Decantr artifacts through `.prettierignore` entries. Tailwind v4 CSS entries receive a marked, receipt-bound `@source not` block for dedicated Decantr paths so generated governance text cannot change the utility bundle; other authored-source mutations remain unapproved.
- For manual pack hydration, prefer `decantr content compile-packs apps/web/decantr.essence.json --write-context`; legacy `decantr registry compile-packs ...` still works.
- MCP agents should use exactly the submitted eight-tool surface: `decantr_project`, `decantr_contract`, `decantr_context`, `decantr_graph`, `decantr_registry`, `decantr_verify`, `decantr_repair`, and `decantr_contract_write`. `decantr_registry` delegates to content-owned implementations; do not expect a ninth content tool in Decantr 3.x.
- Browser evidence is local-only. `decantr verify --base-url <url> --evidence` writes screenshots and Evidence Bundle files under `.decantr/evidence/`.
- CLI telemetry has no Decantr-hosted default. Opt-in is a local preference; network delivery requires an explicit caller-controlled `DECANTR_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT`.

## Packages

- [@decantr/content](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/content): Canonical official corpus, content identity/digest provenance, schemas, API clients, validation, search, resolution, ranking, wiring, and health helpers.
- [@decantr/cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/cli): Workflow commands, contract/context generation, Brownfield/Hybrid governance, Project Health, Studio, CI, and content helpers.
- [@decantr/mcp-server](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/mcp-server): MCP server exposing project state, contracts, context, graph reads, verification, repair prompts, and compatibility content-corpus lookups.
- [@decantr/registry](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/registry): Thin legacy facade over content-owned clients, types, and helpers for Decantr 3.x compatibility.
- [@decantr/essence-spec](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/essence-spec): Essence schemas, validation, migration, and TypeScript types.
- [@decantr/core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/core): Execution-pack compiler, typed graph builders, ranking, evidence/proof ingestion, and Contract capsules.
- [@decantr/verifier](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/verifier): Canonical governed-change contracts plus discovery, audit, critique, Evidence Bundle, loop readiness, authority resolution, diagnostics, and report schemas.
- [@decantr/css](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/css): Legacy optional CSS atom runtime.

## Repositories

- [decantr-ai/decantr](https://github.com/decantr-ai/decantr): Monorepo for packages, API, docs, and official content corpus.
- Historical separate content repo references should point to `packages/content` in the monorepo after 3.8 migration.
